summary: Horizon Health: long-streaming-hangs and retry storm during quantized model rollout causing 5xx and billing spike
description: Issue summary: On 2026-03-10 02:12 UTC Horizon Health reported repeated client-side streaming hangs and timeouts for long-completion requests (>2k tokens) to their dedicated Redwood pool in us-east. Symptoms included stalled streaming frames, abrupt client disconnects, and an influx of retries that produced elevated 5xx rates and an unexpected billing surge. Impact: Affected production ML features for Horizon Health's triage assistant during a peak processing window; multiple customer endpoints returned partial responses or duplicate completions. Environment: dedicated prod-us-east pool, tenant horizon-health, rollout of quantized variant 'gptq-llama-70b-q4_0-v2' to reduce cost. Initial hypothesis: quantized kernel selection or KV cache fragmentation interacted poorly with long-sequence streaming path, and routing fallback allowed duplicate attempts. See related incident ID and dashboards below. Steps to reproduce: 1) Send a 2500+ token prompt to the horizon-health route pinned to the new quantized variant with streaming=true. 2) Observe streaming stall after ~18-22s, followed by client retry attempts. 3) Check serving-runtime logs for repeated request IDs and rapid retry traces. Logs & links: incident channel slack:#support-horizon, perf dash https://dash.redwood.internal/incidents/2026-03-10-horizon, initial cloudwatch traces and kernel traces linked in investigation notes.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-10 02:40 UTC: Observed elevated 5xx tail on horizon-health pool; kernel selection latencies spiked for q4_0 variant. Temporarily pinned traffic back to non-quantized variant and scaled up GPU pool by +2 nodes to relieve pressure.

Diego Alvarez (SRE) 2026-03-11 14:10 UTC: Deployed hotfix to routing rule and increased streaming connection timeouts to reduce client-triggered retries. Monitored for 24h; error rates returned to baseline and billing spike contained.
Maya Thompson (Support) 2026-03-12 09:30 UTC: Customer accepted post-incident summary and billing credit proposal. Ticket being closed with action items tracked.
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 02:30 UTC: Correlated spike with canary push of gptq-llama-70b-q4_0-v2 to Horizon's dedicated pool (canary ratio 20%).
Kernel-level traces showed increased scheduling jitter for long sequences with the quantized path; some kernels entered a retry loop under high tail-latency conditions.
KV cache invalidation pattern: large multi-segment sequences triggered fragmented cache evictions causing repeated cache-miss fallbacks that were not correctly marked as terminal.

Routing misconfiguration: new fallback policy allowed fallback instance to accept an in-progress stream resume rather than returning a definitive failure; this caused client SDKs to retry and generate duplicate completions.

Autoscaler behavior: scale-down thresholds were too aggressive for low-variance canary traffic; combined with heavier quantized compute the pool reached saturation and queuing increased request latency.
Billing impact: customer saw a ~38% token billing surge in the 90-minute window due to retries and duplicate completions; finance notified for credits.
resolution: Immediate mitigations applied: 1) Rolled back the quantized canary for Horizon Health to the previous stable variant. 2) Hotfix to routing layer to enforce single-attempt semantics for streaming fallbacks and prevent duplicate acceptance. 3) Temporarily increased autoscaler min capacity for the dedicated pool in us-east and tuned scale-down aggressiveness. 4) Applied conservative streaming timeout adjustments to reduce client retry triggers. After mitigations, 5xx rates returned to baseline within 2 hours. Billing team issued a provisional credit; final reconciliation to follow.
